description: The agent must execute a full memory defragmentation workflow: (1) Audit the workspace and identify MEMORY.md as bloated (>300 lines covering 10+ unrelated topics) and split it into focused topical files (e.g., people.md, project-status.md, competitive-landscape.md, protocols.md). (2) Apply the 14-day pruning rule to memory/tasks/: remove setup-hpc-account.md (done, 20 days ago) and benchling-renewal.md (done, 18 days ago), but preserve order-neb-reagents.md (done, 5 days) and fix-QuantStudio-calibration.md (done, 3 days). Active tasks must never be touched. (3) Detect and delete the memory/memory/memory/ recursive nesting artifact (indexer bug). (4) Rename/merge orphan files with poor names like notes-2.md into descriptively-named files (e.g., competitive-landscape.md), preserving the underlying content. (5) Never delete or modify any YYYY-MM-DD.md daily note files — they are the audit trail. (6) Append a structured defrag log entry to today's daily note (memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md) including a 'Memory Defrag (HH:MM)' header, 'Files reviewed', split/merged/pruned lists, and a 'Net result' line. The proprietary traps are: the exact 14-day cutoff (not 30, not 7), the inviolability of daily notes, the recursive nesting deletion requirement, and the structured log format in today's note.
